label: <DEL> step, content-weighted (first token b/i/g/p/..., many 1/c/j/v/n/t)
explanation: Fires almost only on the <DEL> step: 99.9% of activation mass is there, with about 29 weak activations on copy step 1. It never fires in the original phase or later in the copy phase. It is active on only about 13% of <DEL> steps, and which ones depends on the sequence content in a graded, additive way. It is more likely to fire, and fires harder, when the first original token (the one about to be output) is b, i, g, p, u, s, d, 0, w or 2 (b is strongest, rate 6.3x), when the original sequence contains many of 1, c, j, v, n, t, and when L is longer (rate rises from 0.6% of steps at L=4 to 1.3% at L=9; t=9 holds 35% of mass). The additive predicate captures 89% of mass on dev with precision 0.32. The rest of the variance looks like a distributed readout of the hidden state at <DEL> that no simple token rule captures.
